name: Acyclovir
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Oral acyclovir is cleared by the kidneys, so the US label lengthens the dosing interval by creatinine clearance (CrCl) and adds a dose after each hemodialysis session. This entry covers oral acyclovir only; intravenous dosing differs.
kidney_function_basis: Label uses creatinine clearance indexed to body surface area (mL/min/1.73 m2).

bands.recommendation: No change for 200 mg or 400 mg regimens (CrCl >10) or 800 mg five times daily (CrCl >25) (label).
800 mg every 4 hours regimen: CrCl 10–25, 800 mg every 8 hours. 200 mg and 400 mg regimens unchanged (CrCl >10) (label).
CrCl 10–25: 800 mg every 8 hours. CrCl 0–10: 200 mg every 12 hours (200 mg and 400 mg regimens) or 800 mg every 12 hours (800 mg regimen) (label).

hd: Adjust schedule so an extra dose is given after each dialysis; a 6-hour session lowers levels by about 60% (label).
pd: No supplemental dose needed after adjusting the interval (label).
crrt: No data in this label. Insufficient data: specialist input.
dialyzable: Yes: half-life about 5 hours during hemodialysis (label).
monitoring: Kidney function, hydration; neurotoxicity risk in kidney impairment.

pediatric.approved_ages: Oral formulations: not established under 2 years (label).
pediatric.usual_dose: Chickenpox, 2 years and older: 20 mg/kg per dose 4 times daily (80 mg/kg/day) for 5 days (label).
pediatric.max_dose: Over 40 kg: adult dose, 800 mg 4 times daily (label).

renal.recommendation: Label renal table is not age-specific and uses mL/min/1.73 m2; no pediatric-specific guidance. Specialist input.

pediatric.egfr_equation: Bedside Schwartz: eGFR (mL/min/1.73 m2) = 0.413 x height (cm) / serum creatinine (mg/dL)
